oneLiner: 用时间与动作研究，把“活儿该怎么干”从老师傅的经验变成可测量、可复制的标准。
oneLinerEn: Study time and motion to turn 'how the job should be done' from craft lore into a measured, repeatable standard.
detail: 弗雷德里克·泰勒从米德维尔和伯利恒钢铁的机修车间起步，1911 年在《科学管理原理》里把“凭经验办事”列为管理的大敌：先用秒表把搬运生铁、铲矿砂的动作逐一分解，测出所谓“一天合理的工作量”，再据最优做法挑选并培训工人、实行差别计件工资，并把计划（方法与定额）同执行（操作）分给不同的人。这是管理第一次成为可被系统研究的对象，工时定额、标准化、职能工长制皆由此而来。它也招致长期批评——工人视之为“把人当机器的提速器”，1912 年国会听证会上劳工证词直指它变相加重劳动强度。吉尔布雷斯夫妇随后把动作研究进一步精细化，而霍桑研究恰好从“人不是经济机器”这一面修正了它，管理学的人性假设由此分岔。
detailEn: Frederick W. Taylor came up through the machine shops of Midvale and Bethlehem Steel and, in The Principles of Scientific Management (1911), named the "rule of thumb" management's great enemy: break pig-iron handling and shoveling into discrete motions with a stopwatch, fix a fair day's pace, then select and train workers against the one best way, pay them on a differential piece rate, and split planning (method, standard) from execution (doing). It was the first moment management became an object of systematic study, bequeathing time standards, standardization and functional foremanship. It drew lasting fire as well—workers called it a speed-up that treated people as machines, and at the 1912 congressional hearing labor testimony charged that it quietly intensified effort. Frank and Lillian Gilbreth refined motion study next, while the Hawthorne studies corrected Taylor from exactly the opposite premise, that people are not economic machines; the human assumption of management theory forked right here.

term: 法约尔：管理五职能与十四条原则
oneLiner: 第一位回答“管理者到底在做什么”的人：计划、组织、指挥、协调、控制。
oneLinerEn: First to answer what a manager actually does: to plan, organise, command, coordinate and control.
detail: 亨利·法约尔 (1916) 从整体组织出发，提出管理的五大职能，以及分工、权责对等、纪律、统一指挥、统一方向、个人利益服从整体、合理报酬、集权、等级链、秩序、公平、人员稳定、首创精神与团队团结等十四条原则。相较关注车间效率的泰勒，他关注的是“管理是一般可教的能力”。
detailEn: Writing in 1916, Henri Fayol took the whole organisation as his unit, naming five functions and fourteen principles — division of work, authority and responsibility, discipline, unity of command and of direction, subordination of self to general interest, fair remuneration, centralisation, scalar chain, order, equity, stability, initiative and esprit de corps. Where Taylor looked at the shop floor, Fayol argued management is a general, teachable skill.

oneLiner: 靠规则、层级、凭技术选才与非人格化管理，换来可预期与公平——代价是可能僵化。
oneLinerEn: Rules, hierarchy, merit selection and impersonal authority buy predictability and fairness — at the price of rigidity.
detail: 马克斯·韦伯描述的“理想型”组织，是把支配从个人恩宠换成非人格规则：清晰分工、成文规则、层级节制、公私分开、依技术资格而非关系任人，管理不带个人好恶。它的力量在于把协作变得可预期、一视同仁且不怕换人——这正是对传统贵族式任人唯亲的革命。但韦伯同时警告它的鬼魂：当规则本身成了目的，就发生“目标置换”，手段（遵守规程）压倒了目的（把事做成），官僚为不犯错而把例外一律拒之门外，反应迟钝。他笔下一贯的冷峻判断是，理性化既是解放也是罩笼——效率与去人格化同时把人锁进铁笼。今天读它不该简化成官僚＝坏：现代医院、民航、审计靠的正是韦伯式无偏好执行，代价则是对例外不敏感——真正的难题在保留一视同仁的同时，给例外留一扇能推开的门。
detailEn: Max Weber's ideal type of organisation replaces personal favour with impersonal rules: clear division of labour, codified rules, a hierarchy, separation of office from person, appointment by technical competence rather than connections, and administration without favouritism. Its strength is making cooperation predictable, equal and durable across the people who leave — a revolution against patrimonial cronyism. But Weber warned of its ghost: when the rule becomes its own end, goal displacement sets in, means (following procedure) outrank the purpose (getting it done), and the bureaucracy, to avoid error, reflexively rejects exceptions and slows to a crawl. His consistent cold judgement was that rationalisation is both liberation and cage: efficiency and depersonalisation also lock people into an iron cage. Reading it today, one should not flatten it to bureaucracy equals bad: modern hospitals, aviation and audit run precisely on Weberian impartial execution, and the cost is insensitivity to the exception — the real puzzle is keeping equal treatment while leaving one door exceptions can push open.

term: 霍桑实验：被关注本身会改变表现
oneLiner: 无论把灯调亮还是调暗，产量都上升——真正起作用的往往是“有人在看着我”。
oneLinerEn: Output rose whether the lights were brightened or dimmed — what mattered was often that someone was paying attention.
detail: 1924 至 1932 年西方电气霍桑工厂的一系列研究：照明实验、继电器装配观察组、庞大访谈计划与接线板班组研究。流传版本是“照明变亮变暗产量都升，所以被关注本身就能提效”（后来叫霍桑效应）。但细账比段子复杂：照明阶段数据根本不稳定，产量提升在非实验期也在发生；真正结实的是接线板组那个发现——群体自定了“合理产量”的规范，并惩罚超速者，非正式组织与同伴压力压过了物质激励。梅奥据此强调人的社会需求与非正式组织，开创了人际关系学派与后来的组织行为学。今天它最有价值的读法是双重的：既提醒实验者与提问者“对象知道被观察就会改变行为”（任何员工调查都有这个噪声），也提醒别把百年前的段子当成当代证据——近年多次重分析连“被关注提效”本身都提出了质疑。
detailEn: The studies ran at Western Electric's Hawthorne Works from 1924 to 1932: illumination tests, the relay assembly observation group, a vast interview programme, and the bank wiring room. The popular version says output rose whether lighting went up or down, so being attended to raises performance — hence 'the Hawthorne effect'. The ledger is messier than the legend: illumination data never stabilised, and output was climbing outside the experiments too. What held up is the bank wiring room finding — the group set its own fair rate of output and sanctioned slackers and rate-busters alike, so informal organisation and peer pressure outranked material incentives. Mayo read from this that workers' social needs and informal groups were the operative variable, founding the human-relations school and, downstream, organisational behaviour. Read it twice today. As a warning to anyone who measures people: subjects who know they are observed behave differently, which is permanent noise in every engagement survey. And as a warning against treating a ninety-year-old anecdote as current evidence — several re-analyses have questioned even the 'attention raises output' claim itself.

oneLiner: 用上下共同设定、可衡量的目标来引导与自我控制，而不是靠事无巨细的命令。
oneLinerEn: Steer and self-control by jointly set, measurable objectives — not by micromanaged orders.
detail: 彼得·德鲁克在《管理的实践》（1954）提出目标管理，三个动作：以成果而非顺从评价人，让员工参与设定清晰可核的目标，并以“自我控制”代替上级遥控。它把管理的重心从“管人管事”转到“管目标与反馈”，也是今天 OKR 的思想源头之一（诺伊米克与杜尔都直认这条谱系）。但要补上两段历史常被删掉的部分：一是德鲁克自己后来抱怨它被用成了“短期业绩考核工具”，忘了前半句“由目的与任务出发”；二是美国企业推行 MBO 的 1960 年代末到七十年代，也是目标被用来压指标、拆部门预算的十年——卡普兰曾指出它因与长期决策脱节而退潮。OKR 算它的第二代修正：目标可以振奋、关键结果必须可核、周期缩短到季度、且评分不直接接薪酬。今天的用法应该同时拿两端：对齐与透明是它最持久的贡献，把目标当命令下达则是它最持久的病。
detailEn: Drucker set out management by objectives in The Practice of Management (1954) with three moves: judge by results rather than compliance, involve people in writing clear and checkable objectives, and substitute self-control for remote supervision. It shifted management from watching people and tasks to aligning goals and feedback, and it is an acknowledged ancestor of OKR — Doerr and Moritz both draw the line back to him, via Intel. Two chapters often deleted deserve restoring. Drucker himself later complained that MBO had been reduced to a short-term appraisal instrument, its first half — deriving objectives from purpose and task — quietly dropped. And the American MBO wave of the late sixties and seventies degenerated into quota-setting and budget slicing; Kaplan attributed its retreat to disconnection from long-range decisions. OKR is best read as its second-generation repair: objectives may inspire, key results must be checkable, the cycle shrinks to a quarter, and scoring deliberately does not feed compensation. Keep both ends in view: alignment and transparency are MBO's most durable contribution, and objectives delivered as orders are its most durable pathology.

term: 系统观点：局部最优未必全局最优
oneLiner: 把组织看作输入—转化—输出—反馈的开放系统，各子系统彼此依存。
oneLinerEn: See the organisation as an open system of input-throughput-output-feedback whose parts depend on each other.
detail: 系统观点源自 1950 年代麻省理工弗雷斯特以《工业动力学》开启的系统动力学，与同期控制论、运筹学交汇，再由圣吉《第五项修炼》在 1990 年代带进管理实践：组织不是零件的堆叠，而是因果的结构——存量与流量、增强与平衡的反馈回路、时间延迟。三条推论随之而来。其一，行为由回路主导而非个人意志：增强回路让强的更强，平衡回路把一切拉回现状，“今日的问题来自昨日的解”是其最尖的一句。其二，延迟制造过度反应：砍客服编制，省钱本季度兑现，流失却在三季度后回——获客成本把省下的吃回去；商业周期与库存鞭打效应都是延迟的反馈。其三，局部最优常是把成本搬到隔壁：仓储间腾挪库存“降低物流费”、端到端的流动却更堵，孤立指标变好而整体变差。于是管理者的问题换掉——不问“该怪谁”而问“哪条回路在主导”，不问“为何不执行”而问“我们奖励了什么结构”。流程管理、约束理论与精益都站在这个前提上。
detailEn: The systems view descends from Forrester's industrial dynamics at MIT in the 1950s, from contemporary cybernetics and operations research, and entered management practice through Senge's 'Fifth Discipline' in the 1990s: an organisation is not a pile of parts but a web of structure — stocks and flows, reinforcing and balancing loops, delays. Three consequences follow. Behaviour is set by which loop dominates, not by anyone's will, hence the sharpest line: 'today's problems come from yesterday's solutions.' Delays breed overreaction — cut service staff and savings land this quarter while the churn wave arrives three quarters later, acquisition costs eating back the win; business cycles and inventory bullwhips are delayed feedback. And local optimisation often displaces rather than creates: a department that 'cuts logistics cost' by shifting stock between warehouses has moved the cost next door, where end-to-end flow worsens while isolated metrics improve. So the manager's questions change: not 'who is to blame' but 'which loop dominates'; not 'why don't they execute' but 'what structure did we reward'. Process management, the theory of constraints and lean all stand on this shared premise.

term: 权变理论：没有最好，只有最合适
oneLiner: 有效的结构与管理方式取决于环境、技术、规模等情境变量。
oneLinerEn: The effective structure and style depend on context — environment, technology, size.
detail: 权变理论是 1960 年代几路实证的共同结论：钱德勒发现美国大企业的结构跟着战略走；伍德沃德按技术复杂度给英国制造商分类（单件、大量、流程），发现管理结构随之而变；劳伦斯与洛尔施比较不同环境的企业（食品、塑料、容器），证明越动荡的环境越靠分化与整合的功夫；伯恩斯与斯托克把两极命名为机械式与有机式；菲德勒则证明没有哪种领导风格包打天下。结论汇成一点：没有最好的组织，只有匹配——维度是环境（稳/变）、技术（单件/大量/流程）、规模与战略。稳定环境奖励集权、正式化、清晰的命令链；动荡与创新环境奖励分权、跨职能、快速迭代。实践含义很硬：抄来的“最佳实践”常常是错配——把大厂的严格绩效体系搬进二十人实验室，会掐死实验室赖以存在的创造力。“权变”也不等于“什么都相对”：责任归属清楚、信息流动通畅、后果与决策匹配，这几条几乎普遍成立。
detailEn: Contingency theory is the shared verdict of 1960s evidence streams: Chandler found American big-company structures had followed their strategies; Woodward, sorting British manufacturers by technical complexity — unit, mass, process — saw appropriate organisation change with it; Lawrence and Lorsch, comparing firms from different environments (foods, plastics, containers), showed turbulent ones live by differentiation and integration; Burns and Stalker named the poles 'mechanistic' and 'organic'; Fiedler demonstrated that no single leadership style wins everywhere. The conclusions converge on one point: there is no best organisation, only fit — along environment (stable or turbulent), technology (unit, mass, process) and scale-and-strategy. Stable settings reward centralisation, formalisation, clean chains of command; turbulent, innovative ones reward decentralisation, cross-functional teams, fast iteration. The practical sting: importing someone else's 'best practice' is usually a fit failure — strict corporate performance regimes dropped into a twenty-person lab can strangle the creativity the lab exists for. Nor does contingency mean 'anything goes': clear accountability, unblocked information flow, and consequences matching decisions hold near-universally.

oneLiner: 源自丰田生产方式：定义价值、让价值流动、由客户拉动、尽善尽美地消除一切不创造价值的浪费。
oneLinerEn: From the Toyota system: define value, make it flow, let the customer pull it, and relentlessly remove waste.
detail: 《改变世界的机器》（1990，沃麦克与琼斯）先用数据证明丰田的造车方式比底特律的大批量生产更省人力、省库存、省出错，沃麦克与琼斯遂在《精益思想》（1996）里把它提炼成五项原则：从客户视角界定价值、沿产品流经识别并打通价值流、让价值不因批次与排队而连续流动、以下游的真实需求拉动上游、循环往复追求尽善尽美。落点是消除日文里的“浪费”——过度生产、等待、搬运、多余加工、缺陷返工、过量库存与不必要的动作都不创造价值。它与约束理论互补：精益盯着让流动更顺的瓶颈，丰田生产方式的两大支柱正是即时化与自动化，大野耐一是这条脉络的枢纽人物。
detailEn: The Machine That Changed the World (Womack and Jones, 1990) first showed with plant-level data that Toyota's way of building cars used less labor, less inventory and produced fewer errors than Detroit's mass production; Womack and Jones then distilled it in Lean Thinking (1996) into five principles: define value from the customer's standpoint, trace and unblock the value stream along the product's journey, let value flow without batching or queueing, pull from the true demand of the downstream step, and repeat toward perfection. The target is muda—overproduction, waiting, transport, extra processing, defects, excess inventory and needless motion create no value. It complements the theory of constraints: lean keeps flow moving through whatever the current bottleneck allows. Just-in-time and autonomation are the two pillars of the Toyota Production System, and Taiichi Ohno is the pivot of this whole lineage.

term: 知识工作者与自我管理
oneLiner: 当资产装在头脑里，靠监工管不住，只能靠目标、自主与持续学习。
oneLinerEn: When the asset lives in people's heads, you cannot supervise it — only aim it, free it and keep it learning.
detail: 德鲁克 1959 年提出“知识工作者”：生产资料随身携带，产出无法被旁观者直接衡量，因而监督天然失效。他说“在知识社会里每个人都要成为自己的管理者”，并把管理者的新任务定为“设计能让知识产生成果的结构”。三重推论今天都落地了：目标必须清得足以自治（于是 OKR），过程无法检查只能检结果与同行评审（于是代码审查、学术审稿），而人才流动的代价极高（离职时把生产资料一起带走）。他还补了一句常被引用的判断：知识工作者的忠诚度归属于专业而非公司，所以雇主必须靠工作本身而非归属词留人。但要两面读：一，“难以衡量”不等于不必衡量，知识工作同样需要问责，否则容易沦为“自主”包装下的产出真空；二，这个称呼本身带幸存者偏差——组内还有大量半知识岗位（客服、运维、内容审核），它们的自主与意义感往往被同一套语言略过。
detailEn: Drucker named the knowledge worker in 1959: the means of production walk out the door every evening, output cannot be judged by standing nearby, and therefore supervision fails by construction. His line that in a knowledge society everyone must become their own manager went with a redefinition of the boss's job — designing a structure in which knowledge yields results. Three consequences have all landed: objectives must be clear enough to run without oversight (hence OKR), process cannot be inspected so results and peers are (hence code review and referee reports), and departure is ruinously expensive because the worker carries the capital. He added a frequently quoted diagnosis: the knowledge worker's loyalty runs to the profession rather than the firm, so the employer must retain by the work itself, not by a language of belonging. Read both sides. Hard-to-measure is not unaccountable; knowledge work still owes an answer, or 'autonomy' becomes a cover for an output vacuum. And the category flatters its members — a large semi-knowledge layer (support, operations, content review) often gets skipped by the same language of autonomy and purpose.

term: 巴纳德：协作系统与权威接受论
oneLiner: 组织是“协作系统”，权威不在头衔，而在下属是否愿意接受指令。
oneLinerEn: An organisation is a cooperative system; authority rests not in the title but in whether subordinates accept the order.
detail: 切斯特·巴纳德《经理人员的职能》(1938) 把组织看作愿为共同目标协作的人的系统，提出权威“接受论”——只有当下属理解、认为与个人利益相符且有能力执行时，命令才真正生效；管理者的三大职能是维持沟通、获取个人服务、界定目标。它是社会系统学派与后来“赋能”思想的先声。
detailEn: In The Functions of the Executive (1938) Chester Barnard saw the organisation as a system of people willing to cooperate toward a common purpose, and proposed the acceptance theory of authority — a command binds only when the subordinate understands it, sees it as consistent with personal interest and can carry it out. The executive's three functions are sustaining communication, securing individual service and defining purpose. It prefigured the social-systems school and today's empowerment thinking.

term: 明茨伯格：管理者十大角色
oneLiner: 管理者不只是“计划组织控制”，而是戴着人际、信息、决策三类十顶帽子。
oneLinerEn: Managers do more than plan-organise-control; they wear ten roles in three families — interpersonal, informational, decisional.
detail: 亨利·明茨伯格 1960 年代末坐在五位总经理身边逐项记录他们真实的一天，发现工作并无经典教科书里计划、组织、控制的那种有序节奏，反而高度碎片化、维持口头传统、偏爱尽快了结的含糊事务。1973 年他在《管理者工作的本质》一文中据观察归纳出十大角色，分属三类：人际的挂名首脑、领导者、联络者；信息的监视者、传播者、发言人；决策的企业家、混乱驾驭者、资源分配者、谈判者。这一框架把“管理”从静态职能还原为动态的角色组合，也解释了为何经理很难像工程师那样被一份岗位说明书框住。后来他对计划学界“精心规划”的祛魅（《战略历程》）与观察如出一辙。
detailEn: In the late 1960s Henry Mintzberg sat beside five chief executives and logged their actual days item by item, finding none of the tidy plan-organize-control rhythm of the textbooks; the work was instead sharply fragmented, oral in habit, and drawn to quick closure, with managers switching topics constantly. From those observations he set out ten roles in The Nature of Managerial Work (1973), grouped into three families: interpersonal (figurehead, leader, liaison), informational (monitor, disseminator, spokesperson) and decisional (entrepreneur, disturbance handler, resource allocator, negotiator). The frame restored "management" from static functions to a dynamic bundle of roles, and explains why a manager resists the job description that binds an engineer. His later disenchantment of elaborate planning (in Strategizing) grew from the same fieldwork.

oneLiner: 日式管理：长期雇佣、缓慢评审、整体关怀与共识决策，以安全换忠诚。
oneLinerEn: The Japanese 'Theory Z': long tenure, gradual review, holistic concern and consensual decisions, trading security for loyalty.
detail: 威廉·大内《Z 理论》(1981) 比较美日企业，主张介于市场型(A)与官僚型(CI)之间的一种形态：稳定雇佣培养归属，集体决策换取执行共识，对员工及其生活整体负责。它呼应麦格雷戈对 X-Y 二分法的超越，也提醒制度需嵌入文化土壤——照搬到高流动、短周期环境常失灵。
detailEn: In Theory Z (1981) William Ouchi compared American and Japanese firms and argued for a form between the market type (A) and the bureaucracy (Cl): stable employment to build belonging, consensual decision-making to buy shared commitment, and concern for the whole employee. It echoes McGregor's move beyond the X-Y split and warns that institutions must sit in cultural soil — transplanted into high-turnover, short-cycle settings it often misfires.

oneLiner: 把泰勒的方法落到车间：移动装配线让汽车越造越快、越卖越便宜，重塑了大众生产与消费。
oneLinerEn: Taylor's ideas hit the shop floor: the moving assembly line made cars ever faster and cheaper to build, reshaping mass production and consumption.
detail: 亨利·福特 1913 年引入移动装配线，把整车装配拆成数百个简单工序、让工件流向工人而非工人绕车转，装配时间骤降；配合“五美元日薪”稳定人手、并让员工买得起车，形成大规模生产—大规模消费的循环。它的代价是高度重复、去技能化与刚性，只适合单一品种的标准化产品。
detailEn: In 1913 Henry Ford ran a moving line, splitting final assembly into hundreds of simple steps with the work flowing to the worker, slashing build time; the 'five-dollar day' steadied labor and let workers buy the cars, fusing mass production with mass consumption. Its price was repetition, deskilling and rigidity suited only to one standardized model.

oneLiner: 被尊为“现代管理理论之母”：她主张用整合取代妥协、以影响而非权力压人，早已预见协作式管理。
oneLinerEn: Hailed as the mother of modern management theory, she urged integration over compromise and influence over coercive power—an early foresight of collaborative management.
detail: 玛丽·帕克·福列特是一战前后活跃在波士顿的社会工作者与管理思想家，其论文汇编为 1924 年的《创造的经验》。她主张冲突未必是你输我赢：除了压制与妥协这两条老路，还有“整合”——把双方真正想要的东西摆上台面，创造出谁都不曾预想的第三种方案，用需求而非立场来谈判。她把领导力的核心定义为“解决问题的技艺”而非权力本身，区分“凌驾于人之上的权力”与“与人共享的权力”，并主张管理者应依专业和情境规律而非职位发号施令。她关于“情境定律”（让规则而非个人来指挥）的设想，半个世纪后才被目标管理、共享领导等重新认领，因而被追认为组织行为学的先声。
detailEn: Mary Parker Follett, a Boston social worker and theorist active around the First World War, left essays gathered in Creative Experience (1924). She argued conflict need not be win-lose: besides domination and compromise there is integration—put each side's real want on the table and invent a third option neither anticipated, negotiating from needs rather than positions. She defined leadership as "the art of solving the problem" rather than power itself, distinguished "power over" from "power with," and urged managers to command by expertise and the law of the situation rather than by rank. Her idea of the "law of the situation"—letting the rule, not a person, give orders—was reclaimed only half a century later by management by objectives and shared leadership, so she is honored today as a forerunner of organizational behavior.

oneLiner: 别修补旧流程，而是推倒重来：以流程为单位、面向客户，追求绩效的跃迁而非渐进改良。
oneLinerEn: Do not patch old steps—start over: work process-by-process, face the customer, seek a leap in performance, not gradual tweaks.
detail: 哈默与钱皮在二十世纪九十年代提出：组织常被职能切成一段段“铁路分段”，没人对整体结果负责。再造要求回到“我们为何做这件事”，围绕端到端流程重新设计，借信息技术合并岗位、并行作业，敢于设定非线性的高目标。它既带来显著提效，也因常被当作裁员的借口、变革剧烈而失败率颇高；但它把流程视角深深植入了后世的管理实践。
detailEn: Hammer and Champy argued in the 1990s that firms are sliced by function into 'railroad segments' with no one owning the whole result. Reengineering returns to why we do the work at all, redesigning end-to-end processes, merging roles and running steps in parallel with IT, and daring nonlinear targets. It brought big gains—and big failures when used as a euphemism for downsizing—yet planted the process lens deep in later practice.

oneLiner: 把二战运筹的数学工具带进管理：用模型、数据与优化替直觉算账，让决策可计算。
oneLinerEn: Carrying wartime operations-research math into management: models, data and optimization compute what intuition guesses, making decisions calculable.
detail: 战后运筹技术转入民用：线性规划（Dantzig 的单纯形法 1947）、排队论（爱尔朗早年的话务模型）、库存模型与网络计划（关键路径与 PERT 都出自五十年代），共同动作是把复杂运营抽象成“目标函数＋约束条件”并求最优。它与西蒙的有限理性恰好互补：一个尽力算得更准，一个提醒算力、信息与模型化的边界。三个坑需要命名：模型把“可量化的”当成“重要的”，于是目标先天偏狭；最优解对参数极敏感，输入小幅拍脑袋就能输出大幅假精确；而模型外的人际关系与非正式约束（霍桑那条线索）它本来就不建模。计算机把这条线推到了今天的数据驱动商业分析：求解器从运货表变成了匹配算法与预测模型，但三张旧面孔一个没变——目标谁定、数据代表谁、模型错了谁负责。
detailEn: Wartime operations research went civilian after 1945: linear programming (Dantzig's simplex method, 1947), queueing theory (Erlang's earlier telephone traffic model), inventory models and network planning (both critical path and PERT born in the fifties), all sharing one move — abstract messy operations into an objective function under constraints and solve for the optimum. It pairs exactly with Simon's bounded rationality: one computes as accurately as it can, the other marks the limits of computing power, information and modelling itself. Three traps deserve naming. Models treat the quantifiable as the important, so the objective is narrow by construction; solutions are hypersensitive to inputs, letting small guesses produce impressive precision; and the informal constraints and relationships that Hawthorne surfaced simply are not in the model. Computing carried the lineage into today's analytics — solvers became matching algorithms and forecasting models — while the three old questions did not change: who sets the objective, whose behaviour the data represents, and who owns the error when the model is wrong.
